permit_authority.value: West Valley City Building Inspection Division
permit_authority.notes: Utah has no single statewide residential solar permitting portal — permitting authority sits with the local municipality (inside its boundaries) or the county (in unincorporated areas). West Valley City's own Building Inspection Division is a separate AHJ from neighboring Salt Lake City (see ut-saltlake-saltlakecity-rmp) despite both being in Salt Lake County.

interconnection_url.notes: See the identical statewide interconnection-tier notes on the Salt Lake City record (ut-saltlake-saltlakecity-rmp) — the same Rocky Mountain Power / Utah PSC three-tier customer classification applies statewide.

required_documents.notes: The City's own Permit Requirements page was referenced by search results but not independently fetched and itemized this session.

value: Residential video inspections are available for select project types, explicitly including solar, per the City's own permitting page

other_conditions: Only a licensed electrical contractor holding an S200 license may pull a residential solar permit — no owner-builder pathway is stated

Per West Valley City Municipal Code 7-7-204: roof-mounted systems must comply with the applicable zone's maximum height requirement (or the roof peak height, if that is lower); ground-mounted systems may not exceed 14 feet in height and are capped at 200 square feet in area, limited to the side or rear yard in residential zones, and treated as accessory structures

Roof-mounted systems must be flush-mounted and parallel to the roof surface where possible; if bracket-mounted or tilted, at least one side of the array must be within 12 inches of the roof surface (or the top of a parapet)
All exterior electrical/plumbing lines for ground-mounted systems must be buried in conduit, except overhead lines near the electric-grid interconnection point
